summary: Meta Newsroom post announcing new LLM-powered controls on Facebook that let users tell the Feed and Reels ranking algorithms, in natural language, what they want to see more or less of. It describes a 'Your algorithm' space for managing topics, follow-up questions after 'Interested'/'Not interested' clicks, and real-time updating within a session. It is vendor copy with no usage data, user evidence, or details on rollout scope.
relevance_reason: It touches on conversational control of an AI system and on personal context (inferred interests plus stated preferences). But it concerns social feed ranking, not voice interfaces, computer-use agents, or personal-context devices. It offers no evidence of how well it works, so it is only a passing, tangential fit.

claims.claim: Meta says new AI tools let users state in their own words what they want in Feed and Reels, and recommendations respond right away.
claims.quote: New AI-powered tools let you tell Facebook, in your own words, what you want to see in Feed and Reels, and your recommendations respond right away.

claims.claim: A new 'Your algorithm' space, reached via the three-dot menu, lets users add and manage topics for Feed and Reels.
claims.quote: We’re rolling out Your algorithm, where you can directly add and manage the topics you want to see in Feed and Reels.

claims.claim: After users click 'Interested' or 'Not interested', Facebook may ask follow-up questions, and recommendations update in real time.
claims.quote: After clicking ‘Interested’ or ‘Not interested,’ we may ask follow up questions for more detail on what you liked or disliked.

claims.claim: Meta says LLMs let the ranking systems use natural-language intent and adapt within the same session. This is a vendor claim with no supporting data.
claims.quote: Tell it what you want more or less of, and your recommendations respond in real time, adapting within the same session to reflect what matters to you right now.

claims.claim: Meta says its existing ranking infers interests from engagement signals such as likes, comments and watch behavior, among thousands of other signals.
claims.quote: inferring what you’re into from what you engage with on Facebook: from the posts you like and comment on to what you watch (among thousands of other signals).

commercial_interest: Vendor speaking about its own product (Meta Newsroom). Promotional framing ('remarkably good', 'genuine leap') with no independent evidence or metrics.
older_event: No. This is a new announcement dated 2026-10-13. Rollout timing and availability by region are not specified.
